article_content: Caroline Stanbury is renowned for her glamorous image and aristocratic background. She's been linked to wealthy figures, including Prince Andrew and footballer Ryan Giggs. She also starred in the reality TV show 'Ladies of London,' showcasing the lives of affluent London socialites. Beyond this, Caroline Stanbury is known for her extravagant collection of designer handbags. Caroline possesses a collection of designer handbags so valuable that a single bag could sustain an average household for several months. Her friends and husband, Cem, acknowledge the extravagance of her collection. In their home's hallway stands a cast-iron statue of a Hermes Birkin bag, symbolizing her passion. Her custom-made walk-in wardrobe houses at least 25 Hermes and Chanel bags. The collection is estimated to be worth around £200,000, with individual Birkin bags costing upwards of £5,000. Some Hermes Kelly bags could cost as much as £25,000, with prices escalating based on size, materials, and customizations. The bags are neatly organized by color and designer, including various Birkin and Kelly bags. Caroline also owns hundreds of shoes by designers like Tom Ford, Gianvito Rossi, Chanel, Givenchy, and Valentino, worth approximately £100,000. She estimates owning 200 pairs of shoes, preferring high-quality items that last. However, handbags remain her true passion. She received her first Birkin bag at 21. Caroline defends her lifestyle, stating that she has worked hard to afford it. She used to buy 'It' bags, sometimes sacrificing other expenses. Now, she prefers classic bags and is a valued customer at Hermes. Her husband supports her passion, even buying her a Chanel Boy bag during a trip to Venice. She believes that a beautiful handbag can elevate an entire outfit, especially when dining in Paris, where Birkin bags are often given their own chair. While she owns 15 Birkin bags, she now favors the smaller and lighter Constance bag. With an estimated personal wealth of £20 million, Caroline emphasizes her strong work ethic. She runs two businesses: Giftlibrary.com and The Wedding Shop of Caroline Stanbury. She acknowledges the stress of running two businesses, despite appearances on television. She entered high society at 17, participating in the Berkeley Dress Show with her mother, a descendant of the Vestey dynasty. Caroline clarifies that her relationship with Prince Andrew was purely platonic. She also dated Ryan Giggs but ended the relationship due to infidelity. She is now married to Cem Habib and has three children. Her background made her an appealing choice for 'Ladies of London,' offering a contrast to the American cast members. She found the first episode difficult to watch. Her mother was initially apprehensive about the show, but Caroline viewed it as a way to gain recognition. Caroline asserts that she has always been driven to succeed, regardless of her husband's wealth. She experienced challenges with Giftlibrary.com, including navigating a double-dip recession. Her success on 'Ladies of London' surprised her, as she wasn't popular in school. Despite her lavish collection, she doesn't expect sympathy. She clarifies that she was not the woman photographed with Prince Andrew in St. Tropez; it was Annabelle Bond.

article_content: Passengers warned of potential delays at Heathrow due to striking workers reported that border controls were 'better than usual'. With Border Agency supervisors filling in for striking airport staff at passport control, passengers expressed their satisfaction with unexpectedly shorter queues. A similar situation unfolded in Dover, where ferry services operated 'well and to time', presenting normal travel conditions. Meanwhile, over half of England's 21,700 state schools were closed, leaving millions of children at home, and thousands of NHS operations and appointments were cancelled. At Heathrow, airport authorities provided complimentary food and water, anticipating significant delays that did not fully materialize. Debbie Arnell, 42, an apprenticeship assessor returning from Philadelphia, noted 'more staff than usual' at passport control in Terminal 5. She added, 'I've used this terminal seven times before, and today was better than usual. They were even giving out free fruit and water, which is unusual. It's almost like they over-compensated.' Richard Bunkham, 45, a human resources consultant from London, described queues at Heathrow's passport control as 'negligible'. Bunkham commented, 'I use iris recognition, so I don't usually experience delays, but it was noticeably better than usual today.' He also stated, 'I think the private sector should also be taking action. I would ask for private sector pensions to be upgraded rather than public sector pensions downgraded.' Noel West, 58, arriving at Terminal 3 from Miami, stated, 'It proves that we do not need half of these people if you can go through as quickly as I did when there is a strike on. It was the fastest I have ever come through passport control. They were really prepared, with clear lines indicating where to go based on passport type, much earlier than usual. However, they did appear to be preparing for longer queues later in the day, providing spare chairs, special invalid chairs, water, and biscuits.' Daily Mail showbiz editor Sara Nathan remarked, 'Heathrow is as dead as a zombie. No queues at immigration at all - but they've laid out water, apples, and Kit-Kats just in case.' Brussels Airlines cancelled one Heathrow to Brussels flight, while Etihad Airways and Aegean Airlines had previously announced cancellations of some Heathrow services. Airport officials had warned passengers of potential delays and provided free food and water as a precaution. BAA reported deploying over 400 additional customer service staff within the terminals, offering 24-hour support, information, food, drinks, and children’s activity packs, equipped with iPads and Blackberries for updates. Critics expressed concerns that the Border Agency strike could compromise national security. However, airport staff reported 'normal levels' of queues, and flights at Heathrow and Gatwick were largely unaffected, with only a few inbound transatlantic flights to Heathrow cancelled earlier. BAA and British Airways reported near-normal services with typical immigration queue lengths. Gatwick Airport reported normal operations for the first 22 inbound flights. The 10 EU UK desks at Terminal 3 immigration were staffed by Home Office personnel and trained police officers, according to the BBC, with five non-EU desks open, suggesting immigration controls were at approximately two-thirds of normal staffing levels. British Airways and BAA spokespersons confirmed a positive start to the day with normal queue lengths, attributing it to effective contingency plans. Gatwick Airport anticipated delays for incoming passengers but had not yet experienced any. The Port of Dover reported all P&O Ferries and DFDS Seaways services running on schedule with available space, and no traffic congestion leading to the port. The PCS union suggested border controls were being manned by a 'hastily gathered' group of police officers, private contractors, and volunteers with limited training. Government figures indicated that over half of England's state schools were closed, with further partial closures, affecting millions of children. Thousands of NHS operations and appointments were cancelled and rescheduled, with emergency and critical care services continuing. The Government estimated approximately 60,000 non-urgent operations, out-patient appointments, tests, and follow-up appointments were postponed in England, while at least 3,000 operations and thousands more hospital appointments were affected in Scotland.

article_content: A new report argues that Britain’s economy cannot thrive unless its ‘mediocre’ education system is significantly improved. The report suggests that failing schools and underperforming teachers lead to a ‘waste of human resources on a large scale,’ negatively impacting the UK's long-term economic health. It also suggests that local councils should not be able to prevent the closure of failing schools, and the teacher assessment system needs reform. Authored by a Nobel Prize-winning economist and former members of the Bank of England, the London School of Economics report advocates for substantial changes to stimulate UK growth. The report also states that ‘short-termist’ banks' reluctance to lend to small businesses is stifling innovation. Furthermore, the report points to ‘years of inadequate investment’ and ‘political delays’ regarding the UK’s aging transport and energy infrastructure as factors hindering growth. The study examined ways to revitalize the UK’s sluggish economy, which is currently on the brink of a triple-dip recession, and ensure long-term growth. The report emphasizes longstanding structural weaknesses in the economy stemming from a failure to achieve stable planning, strategic vision, and political consensus on policies supporting growth, resulting from inadequate investment in skills, infrastructure, and innovation. The potential of many children from disadvantaged backgrounds is being wasted due to underperforming schools. According to the report, failing to provide adequate education to disadvantaged children represents a waste of human resources on a large scale, impeding economic opportunities and hindering growth. Co-author Professor Tim Besley, formerly of the Bank of England, noted the importance of skills for economic growth, suggesting that matching the educational standards of Australia or Finland could significantly increase UK income. He proposed extending teachers’ probation periods from two to four years and shifting assessment towards on-the-job evaluation rather than initial career assessments. Professor Tim Besley also emphasized the need to improve educational outcomes for disadvantaged children, particularly those on free school meals, as a key driver of economic growth. The report suggests allowing underperforming schools to gradually reduce in size by admitting fewer students each year, while enabling successful schools to expand. It also calls for local councils to facilitate the shrinking of failing schools and the expansion of successful ones. The report identifies vocational skills as ‘particularly underdeveloped’ and advocates for increased access through more apprenticeships. The report also suggests that the UK’s economic recovery is dependent on banks resuming lending to small businesses. A lack of competition among lenders is hindering essential investment in innovation and impeding recovery. The government should facilitate the entry of new banks into the market, and, as a last resort, consider breaking up major banks like Lloyds and RBS to foster competition. The report highlights that despite cutting-edge science, small and medium-sized enterprises struggle to access funding for their ideas. It suggests prioritizing small British firms with high growth potential through the government’s Business Bank. Professor Tim Besley reiterated the need to match the educational standards of countries like Australia or Finland. The report proposes easing banking license requirements and removing barriers to entry to increase the pool of lenders for businesses. Professor Besley stated that breaking up existing banks should only be considered as a last resort if other measures to improve lending are unsuccessful. The report criticizes ‘repeated political delays’ on critical infrastructure projects. It points to airport capacity in the South East as a prime example of political hesitation jeopardizing London’s status as a major hub. The report recommends establishing a new infrastructure strategy board to prioritize essential projects and an infrastructure bank to secure funding. It also notes that the UK has consistently failed to build enough houses to meet demand and suggests introducing road tolls to alleviate congestion. In response to the report, Business Secretary Vince Cable stated that the government is implementing an industrial strategy in partnership with businesses to address the issues identified by the LSE’s Growth Commission report. Cable emphasized the need for continued investment in skills and innovation, highlighting the £1billion business bank and a £75million investment package for research-intensive SMEs, as well as investments in apprenticeships and deregulation efforts to stimulate economic growth.

También sugiere que los consejos locales no deberían poder evitar el cierre de escuelas deficientes, y que el sistema de evaluación de maestros necesita una reforma. Escrito por un economista ganador del Premio Nobel y antiguos miembros del Banco de Inglaterra, el informe de la London School of Economics aboga por cambios sustanciales para estimular el crecimiento del Reino Unido. El informe también afirma que la reticencia de los bancos ‘cortoplacistas’ a prestar a las pequeñas empresas está frenando la innovación. Además, el informe señala ‘años de inversión inadecuada’ y ‘retrasos políticos’ con respecto al envejecimiento de la infraestructura de transporte y energía del Reino Unido como factores que obstaculizan el crecimiento. El estudio examinó formas de revitalizar la lenta economía del Reino Unido, que actualmente está al borde de una recesión de triple caída, y garantizar el crecimiento a largo plazo. El informe enfatiza las debilidades estructurales de larga data en la economía derivadas de la falta de planificación estable, visión estratégica y consenso político sobre las políticas que apoyan el crecimiento, como resultado de una inversión inadecuada en habilidades, infraestructura e innovación. El potencial de muchos niños de entornos desfavorecidos se está desperdiciando debido a las escuelas de bajo rendimiento. Según el informe, no proporcionar una educación adecuada a los niños desfavorecidos representa un desperdicio de recursos humanos a gran escala, lo que impide las oportunidades económicas y obstaculiza el crecimiento. El coautor, el profesor Tim Besley, anteriormente del Banco de Inglaterra, destacó la importancia de las habilidades para el crecimiento económico, sugiriendo que igualar los estándares educativos de Australia o Finlandia podría aumentar significativamente los ingresos del Reino Unido. Propuso extender los períodos de prueba de los maestros de dos a cuatro años y cambiar la evaluación hacia la evaluación en el trabajo en lugar de las evaluaciones iniciales de la carrera. El profesor Tim Besley también enfatizó la necesidad de mejorar los resultados educativos de los niños desfavorecidos, en particular los que reciben comidas escolares gratuitas, como un impulsor clave del crecimiento económico. El informe sugiere permitir que las escuelas de bajo rendimiento se reduzcan gradualmente en tamaño admitiendo menos estudiantes cada año, al tiempo que se permite que las escuelas exitosas se expandan. También pide a los consejos locales que faciliten la reducción de las escuelas deficientes y la expansión de las exitosas. El informe identifica las habilidades vocacionales como ‘particularmente subdesarrolladas’ y aboga por un mayor acceso a través de más aprendizajes. El informe también sugiere que la recuperación económica del Reino Unido depende de que los bancos reanuden los préstamos a las pequeñas empresas. La falta de competencia entre los prestamistas está obstaculizando la inversión esencial en innovación e impidiendo la recuperación. El gobierno debería facilitar la entrada de nuevos bancos en el mercado y, como último recurso, considerar la posibilidad de dividir los principales bancos como Lloyds y RBS para fomentar la competencia. El informe destaca que, a pesar de la ciencia de vanguardia, las pequeñas y medianas empresas tienen dificultades para acceder a la financiación para sus ideas. Sugiere dar prioridad a las pequeñas empresas británicas con un alto potencial de crecimiento a través del Banco de Negocios del gobierno. El profesor Tim Besley reiteró la necesidad de igualar los estándares educativos de países como Australia o Finlandia. El informe propone facilitar los requisitos de la licencia bancaria y eliminar las barreras de entrada para aumentar el grupo de prestamistas para las empresas. El profesor Besley declaró que la división de los bancos existentes sólo debería considerarse como último recurso si otras medidas para mejorar los préstamos no tienen éxito. El informe critica los ‘repetidos retrasos políticos’ en los proyectos de infraestructura críticos. Señala la capacidad aeroportuaria en el sudeste como un excelente ejemplo de la vacilación política que pone en peligro la condición de Londres como centro importante. El informe recomienda establecer una nueva junta de estrategia de infraestructura para priorizar los proyectos esenciales y un banco de infraestructura para asegurar la financiación. También señala que el Reino Unido no ha logrado construir suficientes viviendas para satisfacer la demanda y sugiere la introducción de peajes para aliviar la congestión. En respuesta al informe, el Secretario de Negocios, Vince Cable, declaró que el gobierno está implementando una estrategia industrial en asociación con las empresas para abordar los problemas identificados por el informe de la Comisión de Crecimiento de la LSE. Cable enfatizó la necesidad de una inversión continua en habilidades e innovación, destacando el banco de negocios de £1 mil millones y un paquete de inversión de £75 millones para las PYMES intensivas en investigación e innovación, así como inversiones en aprendizajes y esfuerzos de desregulación para estimular el crecimiento económico.

article_content: Fans of the women's surf-wear brand Roxy have expressed outrage at a new teaser video, deeming it demeaning to women. The video has been branded 'disrespectful' and 'disappointing', with some viewers feeling 'utterly disgusted'. Posted on Roxy's YouTube channel and Facebook page, the short video features a faceless female surfer preparing to hit the waves; however, focus is predominantly on her posterior. Furthermore, the video concludes as she paddles out to sea, omitting any actual surfing, which has dissatisfied fans. The controversial video is the official teaser for the Roxy Pro Biarritz 2013 poster girl reveal (Australian pro-surfer Stephanie Gilmore). Critics argue the surfer is portrayed as a sexual object rather than a talented athlete. Facebook user Marlaina Read commented: 'Women are multidimensional, yet this video reduces a pro surfer, athlete, and mentor to her sexual appearance... So original! It's hard enough getting coverage for women's sport, and this opportunity to showcase the competition and the surfers' abilities has been wasted. Sitting on your bed in your undies and sexily undressing for a shower is in no way a dimension.' Another Facebook user, Wendy McGirr, wrote: 'I'm not bothered by sexy commercials; sex sells. However, I am bothered that you promote a world tour surfing event focusing entirely on a woman's butt. Aimed at whom?! Not women, that's for sure. It should be about their talent, athleticism, and power. Amazed ASP still lets sponsors do this in 2013. It wouldn't happen at Wimbledon. Totally uninspiring.' Marlaina Read added: 'It should have gotten my attention by showing her awesome surfing skill. Instead, it disappointed me by reducing women to their sexuality, yet again.' Ngai Min Ching stated: 'Utterly disgusted that a brand promoting natural beauty with a vast female client base focuses so much on sexualizing a female athlete's body when promoting a world surfing event. Not a single surfing shot was displayed, yet it was meant to promote surfing talents! I was a big Roxy fan until I saw your response... We KNOW she is sexy; we know she has an amazing body; but do you have no other selling points to attract interest to Roxy Pro Biarritz? Pathetic, really.' Others defended the brand, arguing that male surfers face similar objectification and the video at least drew attention to the competition. Molly Misetich noted: 'I would just like to point out that male surfers are shirtless and have their butts showing through their board shorts all the time during contests, and somehow that's not sexist? As a very proud surfer girl, I do wish the video had an ounce of surfing in it (come on Roxy), but the video got everyone's attention. It may have been for the wrong reasons, but it got attention. With that I bet many more people will be watching the contest than before... And to say that the company that made the first women's board shorts is sexist and is setting us back, in my opinion, is just stupid.' Roxy responded on their Facebook page: 'Whether you are athletic, smart, funny, sexy, daring, confident - we support whatever combination you choose to be. Women are complex and multidimensional. To ignore this fact is to ignore who we truly are. Obviously, there's been much conversation around the video we recently released. We believe all athletes are naturally beautiful, in and out of the water. You certainly don't have to be sexy to be an athlete, and we also believe it's not wrong to be an athlete and to be sexy, if you choose to be. We don't judge one to be better than the other and we don't believe in excluding one for the other. Thank you for the passionate thoughts shared on the video, and for expressing how much you respect women in surfing.'

article_content: A recent photograph released by North Korea, seemingly showcasing a powerful display of military hovercraft, has come under scrutiny. Initially appearing to represent a combat-ready force amid escalating tensions with the United States, the image aligns with the Communist nation's warnings of a potential offensive to overturn the Korean War armistice of 60 years ago. However, closer inspection suggests digital manipulation. The photo, distributed by the Korean Central News Agency and widely circulated internationally, purportedly depicted hovercraft landing on North Korea's east coast. Accompanying the vehicles were troops from the Korean People's Army and Navy, observed by leader Kim Jong-un. Photographic expert Alan Taylor argues that the image was likely doctored. In his analysis for Atlantic magazine's In Focus, Taylor points out that two of the closest hovercraft appear to be duplicates, digitally copied and pasted. He also notes that other craft in the distance exhibit characteristics of digital manipulation, such as mismatched colors and soft edges. Meanwhile, in South Korea, military exercises were underway. Tanks were deployed in Pocheon, situated approximately 28 miles northeast of Seoul and nine miles south of the demilitarized zone that divides the two countries. This incident isn't the first accusation of North Korea manipulating images for propaganda. A previous photo from Kim Jong-il's funeral in 2011 was also allegedly altered to remove journalists, creating the illusion of undivided attention on the event. Tensions have escalated between the two Koreas following North Korea's recent nuclear test, which triggered UN sanctions. Images show various military activities, including rocket launches and Kim Jong-un overseeing beach landing exercises, surrounded by military officials and female soldiers.
translated_content: Una fotografía reciente publicada por Corea del Norte, que aparentemente muestra una imponente exhibición de aerodeslizadores militares, ha sido objeto de escrutinio. Inicialmente, la imagen parecía representar una fuerza lista para el combate en medio de las crecientes tensiones con Estados Unidos, lo que coincide con las advertencias del régimen comunista sobre una posible ofensiva para revocar el armisticio de la Guerra de Corea de hace 60 años. Sin embargo, una inspección más detallada sugiere manipulación digital. La foto, distribuida por la Agencia Central de Noticias de Corea y ampliamente difundida a nivel internacional, supuestamente mostraba aerodeslizadores aterrizando en la costa oriental de Corea del Norte. Acompañando a los vehículos, había tropas del Ejército Popular y la Armada de Corea, bajo la atenta mirada del líder Kim Jong-un. El experto en fotografía Alan Taylor argumenta que es probable que la imagen haya sido manipulada. En su análisis para la sección In Focus de la revista Atlantic, Taylor señala que dos de los aerodeslizadores más cercanos parecen ser duplicados, copiados y pegados digitalmente. También señala que otras embarcaciones en la distancia exhiben características de manipulación digital, como colores dispares y bordes difuminados. Mientras tanto, en Corea del Sur, se estaban llevando a cabo ejercicios militares. Se desplegaron tanques en Pocheon, situado a unos 45 kilómetros al noreste de Seúl y a unos 14 kilómetros al sur de la zona desmilitarizada que divide a las dos Coreas. Este incidente no es la primera acusación de manipulación de imágenes por parte de Corea del Norte con fines propagandísticos. Una foto anterior del funeral de Kim Jong-il en 2011 también fue supuestamente alterada para eliminar a periodistas, creando la ilusión de una atención exclusiva sobre el evento. Las tensiones se han intensificado entre las dos Coreas tras la reciente prueba nuclear norcoreana, que desencadenó sanciones por parte de la ONU. Corea del Norte también ha expresado su enojo por los ejercicios militares conjuntos realizados por Estados Unidos y Corea del Sur. article_content: Legislation essential for initiating the £50 billion HS2 high-speed rail project, designed to connect London with the North, has received approval. This ‘paving Bill,’ formally known as the High Speed Rail (Preparation) Act 2013, has been authorized by the Queen, enabling preparatory construction work. Prime Minister David Cameron hosted a gathering of civic leaders who voiced their support for the railway. Despite its promise, the project is affecting many homeowners along its path, yet Cameron declared it beneficial for the entire nation. The approved law permits the government to allocate funds for detailed planning of the HS2 route and for acquiring properties from affected residents and businesses. The comprehensive construction plan is expected to be released early next week. This progress coincided with a meeting between Prime Minister Cameron and a group of council leaders at Downing Street, where they pledged their support for the £50 billion high-speed rail initiative. They posed with a banner proclaiming ‘High Speed Rail for High Speed Cities’. Following the meeting, Manchester City Council leader Sir Richard Leese remarked that HS2 would greatly benefit regional cities, creating a win-win situation for all, including London. Transport Secretary Patrick McLoughlin also attended the meeting. The project's second phase aims to extend the line from Birmingham to the northwest and northeast of England by 2032/33. Sir Richard expressed his desire to experience the high-speed line from Manchester within his lifetime. Birmingham City Council leader Sir Albert Bore stated that Cameron agrees the project is about boosting capacity and providing economic advantages nationwide. Leeds City Council member James Lewis wishes the second phase would begin sooner, highlighting HS2 as crucial for the country's growth, given the lack of plans for new motorways. In Parliament, Cheryl Gillan expressed her constituents' concerns regarding the royal assent to the Bill, which she believes will negatively affect those in Chesham and Amersham. This statement was made during a debate on stalking, following Deputy Speaker Eleanor Laing's announcement. HS2 Ltd chief executive Alison Munro said the Paving Bill's approval is a vital step, allowing the project to advance with early ground investigations and private sector collaboration for skills and training development in anticipation of HS2's delivery. The £50 billion project plans to link London and Birmingham by 2026, followed by extensions to Manchester and Leeds, via Sheffield, by 2033.

article_content: A 16-year-old boy from Washington State was in a precarious situation on Monday night after spending five hours stuck in a bog. The unidentified teenager was at a skate park in Puyallup when he and a friend decided to wander into a restricted woodland area around 1 p.m. While attempting to cross a shallow stream, he sank thigh-high into muddy ground. Central Pierce Fire and Rescue spokesman Ed Hrivnak told Kiro TV that the mud was deceiving: 'He was trying to cross, and looking from above, you’d think you’d sink to your foot. 'But it was very deceiving, and when he stepped he sunk all the way to his thigh.' Knowing they were in an area where they shouldn't be, the teen's friend initially resisted calling for help. He spent several hours attempting the rescue himself but eventually walked to a local fire department for assistance. Crews managed to free the trapped boy around 6 p.m. They used ladders to stabilize the area around him and used air and water pressure to free his legs. According to authorities, the boy was cold and muddy but otherwise uninjured. After being cleared by paramedics, he was taken home by his mother. Footage shows the boy being pulled from the mud in the dark and giving a firefighter a hug as he wobbles.

article_content: A crossword writer has been accused of hiding a coded message to assassinate President Hugo Chavez's brother within a newspaper puzzle. Venezuelan intelligence agents interviewed Neptali Segovia after a state TV pundit suggested his clues revealed a secret message to assassinate Chavez's brother, Adan. This incident is the latest in a series of bizarre political stories emerging from Venezuela, which is experiencing a particularly tense year leading up to its elections. Answers to the crossword included 'Adan' (Chavez's brother), 'asesinen' (meaning 'kill'), and 'rafaga' (which can mean either a burst of gunfire or a gust of wind). 'These types of messages were frequently used during World War Two,' said pundit Perez Pirela earlier this week in a dramatic denouncement of Ultimas Noticias newspaper on live television. The puzzle, published on Wednesday, included answers such as 'Adan,' 'asesinen,' and 'rafaga'. Mr. Pirela, who uses his early evening TV show to criticize Chavez's opponents, stated that mathematicians, psychologists, and others had studied the Spanish-language crossword and concluded it was a coded assassination plot. Ultimas Noticias reported that six officers from Venezuela's intelligence service visited the newspaper's editorial offices on Thursday seeking information about Segovia. The newspaper added that Segovia voluntarily went to the intelligence service's headquarters to provide a statement. The accusation highlights the dangerously polarized environment in Venezuela, where the socialist incumbent Chavez has been accusing opposition leaders of planning violence ahead of October's presidential vote. Uncertainty surrounding Chavez's health condition has only heightened the tense atmosphere in the country. Pirela pointed out that French leader Charles de Gaulle used to broadcast coded messages from London to Resistance fighters in France during World War Two. 'It's a message... I'm speaking in the name of truth,' Pirela added. Neptali Segovia was interviewed by intelligence officers after creating a puzzle that had some violent-sounding answers. Segovia insisted on his innocence, stating in the newspaper: 'I am the first to want to clarify this. I have nothing to hide because the work I have been doing for the last 17 years has only a cultural and educational intention, and is transparent.' 'I was treated respectfully. They took down my comments and made a routine summary. Then they took me home,' he said. Crosswords appear to be a political tool, as another newspaper, the militantly pro-opposition Tal Cual, lampooned the Chavez government on Friday with a front-page game highlighting the nation's ills. Clues included: 'What officials do when they misuse public funds' (Corruption); 'Perhaps the most abused law?' (Constitution); and 'Name of supreme leader who governs our destiny? Bearded.' (Fidel Castro).

(Constitución); y '¿Nombre del líder supremo que gobierna nuestro destino? Barbudo.' (Fidel Castro).

article_content: This World Cup hasn't favored reputations. It also hasn't revealed a clear frontrunner for the title. Argentina is a contender, but its performances have shown fragility. Still, it keeps winning and faces either the United States or Belgium in the quarterfinals. Switzerland nearly toppled Argentina, but like Bosnia and Herzegovina, Iran, and Nigeria, a moment of brilliance decided Tuesday's match. With the game seconds from penalties, Lionel Messi of Barcelona drove into Swiss territory and passed to Real Madrid's Angel Di Maria, who scored. Blerim Dzemaili's late header hit the post, underscoring Switzerland's agony. Argentina's reaction at the final whistle showed relief. Messi said, 'I was nervous because we couldn't score and any mistake could have knocked us out. We were suffering, but we had a special play; I passed to Angel, and now we can celebrate.' Switzerland aimed to limit Argentina's attacking space. Messi had an early chance, but his shot was saved. As the game progressed, Switzerland gained confidence due to Argentina's subdued offense. Xherdan Shaqiri found Granit Xhaka, whose shot was saved by Sergio Romero. Ezequiel Lavezzi tested Benaglio after a pass from Gonzalo Higuain. Shaqiri then set up Josip Drmic, who chipped the ball poorly. Romero looked uncertain, spilling a Shaqiri free kick. Argentina attacked more as the hour approached. Benaglio saved a shot from Marcos Rojo and a header from Higuain. Messi's attempt went over the bar. Benaglio then saved Messi's shot in the 78th minute. Switzerland held on, aiming for extra time. Rodrigo Palacio's header was saved, and Messi avoided a booking. Di Maria tested Benaglio before scoring the winner from a Messi pass. Dzemaili then hit the post with a header. Shaqiri won a late free kick, but the final whistle blew. Coach Alejandro Sabella said, 'Our dream is to work for the next match and try to move onto the semifinals. We do not look beyond that.' Argentina advances, and winning without playing perfectly is acceptable if it leads to its first World Cup since 1986.

El cabezazo tardío de Blerim Dzemaili golpeó el poste, subrayando la agonía de Suiza. La reacción de Argentina al silbatazo final fue de alivio. Estábamos sufriendo, pero tuvimos una jugada especial; le pasé el balón a Ángel y ahora podemos celebrar'. Suiza apuntó a limitar el espacio de ataque de Argentina. Shaqiri luego asistió a Josip Drmic, quien intentó un globito sin éxito. Romero parecía inseguro, rechazando un tiro libre de Shaqiri. Argentina atacó más a medida que se acercaba la hora. Benaglio detuvo un disparo de Marcos Rojo y un cabezazo de Higuaín. El intento de Messi pasó por encima del travesaño. Benaglio luego detuvo el disparo de Messi en el minuto 78. article_content: Leaders from Pacific nations will meet in San Francisco for the 2023 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit next week. The U.S. Secret Service has developed a plan to counter potential threats amid increased global tensions. Given ongoing wars in several regions and a heightened threat environment, Secret Service leaders, the agency responsible for the event's security, emphasize they are taking every precaution. 'We're constantly monitoring the current environment and potential threats,' Secret Service Director Kim Cheatle told ABC News. 'Over the past few years, we've seen groups, demonstrators, or individuals using large-scale events to draw attention or convey their message. The Secret Service respects the right of people to demonstrate peacefully.' The Secret Service is collaborating with the FBI and other intelligence agencies, and will 'adjust our security posture accordingly' in coordination with local law enforcement, according to Cheatle. The Department of Homeland Security has designated APEC as a National Special Security Event (NSSC), placing the Secret Service in charge of planning and coordinating security. Other NSSC events include the Super Bowl and the United Nations General Assembly. Cheatle stated that the Secret Service deploys significant resources to secure major events like APEC. 'We provide personnel, technical assets, and various resources,' she said. Law enforcement officials have expressed particular concern about the threat of lone wolf actors. Cheatle noted that because protecting the president is a primary duty of Secret Service agents, they are well-prepared to address this threat. 'It's important to remember that the Secret Service protects the president at events daily, which is always a focus. This event is larger in size and scope, so we may deploy different or additional assets to mitigate potential threats. The Secret Service is very aware of this every day,' she said. Twenty-one heads of state are expected to attend APEC, including President Joe Biden and Chinese President Xi Jinping. They are expected to meet during the summit. China's attendance is notable given its increasingly assertive actions in the Indo-Pacific. According to U.S. intelligence, Xi has instructed his military to 'be ready by 2027' to invade Taiwan.

article_content: During opening statements on Wednesday in the criminal trial concerning FTX's downfall, Sam Bankman-Fried's lawyer, Mark Cohen, pointed the finger at Caroline Ellison, Bankman-Fried's former girlfriend. Cohen asserted that Bankman-Fried placed his trust in Ellison, the one-time CEO of Alameda Research, FTX's sister company, to manage the organization and implement protective measures when investing funds that were transferred between the two entities. As cryptocurrency values decreased, Cohen stated, Bankman-Fried urged Ellison to protect Alameda Research from significant financial losses by hedging its positions. However, Ellison reportedly disregarded this advice. Bankman-Fried is currently on trial in Manhattan federal court, facing allegations that he defrauded FTX's clientele and investors of billions of dollars. Insider contacted Ellison's legal representative for comment, but received no immediate response. According to a recent biography, Ellison and Bankman-Fried had an intermittent romantic relationship spanning at least three years. Ellison, who has already admitted guilt to fraud charges and has been cooperating with authorities since December, is anticipated to be a key witness in the proceedings. Furthermore, Bankman-Fried has previously attempted to shift responsibility for the platform's failure onto Ellison and other executives. He even shared excerpts from Ellison's personal journal with The New York Times in July. Cohen also stated on Wednesday that Bankman-Fried believed the company would be able to fully repay its lenders on schedule and that he 'acted in good faith and took reasonable business measures.' Reuters reported that Bankman-Fried's attorney depicted the former FTX CEO as a 'math nerd' who failed to adequately consider risk management during his statements. The lawyer also emphasized the crypto market's unpredictable nature, which he claimed was a major complicating factor for startups like FTX. Cohen remarked, 'It's not a crime to run a business.' Meanwhile, prosecutor Thane Rehn informed the jury that Bankman-Fried misappropriated over $10 billion from FTX users, while assuring them they could withdraw their funds at any moment. Rehn stated, 'When customers put money in FTX, he stole it. When they put crypto in, he stole that too.' The trial commenced on Tuesday and could last for up to six weeks. Bankman-Fried is charged with seven counts of fraud. A conviction could result in a substantial prison sentence.

article_content: Bolivian President Evo Morales is well-known for his critical stance on the U.S. government. He voiced his complaints to a global audience at the U.N. General Assembly, advocating for action against the Obama administration. Morales suggested the formation of a 'Tribunal of the People,' involving international bodies and human rights advocates, to initiate legal action against the Obama government. He made this proposition during a speech on Tuesday. Earlier in the month, Morales declared that Bolivia would accuse the U.S. of committing crimes against humanity in international courts. While his remarks might be seen as exaggerated rhetoric, they represent a significant critique of the U.S. on a prominent international stage. Morales's approach aligns with a pattern of strong criticisms delivered at the United Nations by various Latin American countries with leftist administrations. The late Venezuelan President Hugo Chavez famously referred to George W. Bush as the devil at the same podium in 2006, adding that the location still carried a 'smell of sulfur.' Chavez's accusation seven years prior was that Bush was acting 'as if he owned the world.' Morales echoes a similar sentiment, directing his criticism toward Obama. Morales told CNN en EspaÃ±ol on Thursday that the U.S. engages in 'aerial piracy' by restricting airspace usage or limiting visa approvals for delegations from disfavored nations. He also stated, 'Sometimes, they limit our visas,' and 'They blackmail us with visas.' Morales cited allegations by the Venezuelan government that its president, Nicolas Maduro, was prevented from flying over U.S. airspace the previous week, claiming the U.S. denies airspace access and then provides false explanations. U.S. officials asserted that the matter had been resolved satisfactorily, though Maduro viewed the incident as disrespectful. According to Morales, the Obama government promotes democracy while behaving like a dominant global power. He stated, 'First, he talks about peace... but he does not contribute to peace.' During his address to the assembly earlier in the week, Obama focused on Iran and the Middle East, with limited attention to Latin America. However, he acknowledged criticisms against the U.S. for intervening in other nations' affairs, particularly in the Middle East. Obama noted that 'The United States is chastised for meddling in the region, and accused of having a hand in all manner of conspiracy,' and 'At the same time, the United States is blamed for failing to do enough to solve the region's problems, and for showing indifference toward suffering Muslim populations.' Morales attended the U.N. meeting in New York, whereas Maduro did not, citing alleged plots against him. Due to concerns over safety in New York, Morales proposed rotating the U.N. General Assembly to other locations, such as Switzerland or Brazil.

article_content: Tunisian politician Beji Caid Essebsi has won the country's first free presidential election. Essebsi won with 55.68% of the vote against incumbent Moncef Marzouki's 44.32% in the run-off ballot, marking a final step in the transition to democracy after the 2011 uprising that ousted Zine El-Abidine Ben Ali. The electoral authorities released the results today. A former official under Ben Ali, Essebsi rebranded himself as a technocrat, and his secular party Nidaa Tounes (Call for Tunisia) profited from a backlash against the post-revolution Islamist government, which many voters blamed for the turmoil after 2011. Hundreds of jubilant supporters celebrated outside Nidaa Tounes headquarters in Tunis, waving Tunisian flags, singing, and honking car horns. Essebsi supporter Aya Khiari said: 'We succeeded in part of our struggle. These elections were just one round, but the battle to build Tunisia has just started.' Marzouki made no immediate statement, but his campaign's official Facebook page indicated that he had congratulated Essebsi. Protesters set fire to a Nidaa Tounes party office in Tataouine, southern Tunisia, immediately after results were announced. Rioting also occurred in Hamma, another southern town, where police used teargas to disperse youths who burned tyres in protest against the return of Ben Ali's old guard. Critics view Essebsi, an 88-year-old former parliamentary speaker under Ben Ali, as a setback for the 2011 uprising that led the North African country to full democracy with a new constitution and free elections. The Tunisian uprising inspired the Arab Spring revolts across North Africa and the Middle East. U.S. President Barack Obama and U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry congratulated Essebsi and Tunisia on the conclusion of the first presidential election under the new constitution. Kerry stated: 'Tunisia has provided a shining example to the region and the world of what can be achieved through dedication to democracy, consensus, and an inclusive political process.' Compromise has been important in Tunisian politics. Essebsi's Nidaa Tounes reached a deal with the Islamist Ennahda party to overcome a political crisis triggered by the murder of two secular leaders last year. As frontrunner, Essebsi dismissed critics who said his victory would mark a return of the old guard, distancing himself from the corruption and abuses of Ben Ali's era. He argued that he was the technocrat Tunisia needed following three years of an Islamist-led coalition government. Marzouki, who sought refuge in France during the Ben Ali era, portrayed a potential Essebsi presidency as a reverse for the 'Jasmine Revolution'. Many tied Marzouki to the Ennahda government. Accepting former regime officials - known as the 'Remnants' by their critics - back into politics had been one of the compromises that helped restore calm and keep Tunisia's transition to democracy on track. Victory for Essebsi consolidates Nidaa Tounes' position after it won the most seats in October's parliamentary election, beating out the Islamist party Ennahda. Essebsi's party will now decide on a prime minister and form a new coalition government before tackling Tunisia's low-level Islamist militancy and politically sensitive economic reforms. Ennahda holds the second largest number of seats and, along with the leftist Popular Front movement, will prove tough opponents in policy negotiations in parliament. (Editing by Angus MacSwan and Dominic Evans)

article_content: Botox is known to diminish frown lines, prevent migraines, and even alleviate excessive sweating. Now, some women are seeking off-label uses for the injectable to extend the duration of their blow-outs. According to Yahoo Beauty, this procedure is gaining popularity among women who want to 'attend SoulCycle without getting their hair sweaty'. Leading New York dermatologist Dr. Patricia Wexler notes that improved hair quality is a beneficial side effect of Botox's impact on sweat glands. Is this an extreme solution for frizz-free hair? Botox is now being injected into the scalp to help patients maintain their blow-dries for a longer period. 'It works just like injections for hyperhidrosis,' she told Dailymail.com. '[Botox] specifically inhibits the eccrine glands.' The result of reduced scalp perspiration is that patients may experience less frizz and require less frequent hair washing. Dr. Wexler acknowledges that the cost of the procedure can be 'prohibitive' but would recommend it if a patient inquired. 'It has few side effects when administered in a safe dilution and dose,' she explains. 'It should be carefully placed along the hairline and frontal area where frizz is most noticeable.' Yahoo reports that treating an entire scalp would require over 100 units of Botox, with effects lasting up to three months. However, Dr. Wexler advises against using Botox on the entire head, as it 'would not be practical from a cost or safety perspective.' While Dr. Wexler has never injected an entire scalp, dermatologist Dr. Francesca Fusco told Yahoo that 'several women whose foreheads I have injected happily report decreased sweating at the hairline and temples.' In contrast, dermatologist Dr. Neal Schultz argues that the procedure is painful, expensive, and not sufficiently effective to justify its cost to the patient. He explained to Yahoo that injecting only the hairline will not prevent sweating on other areas of the scalp. Therefore, the remaining hair may still become frizzy or limp after exercising. Moreover, the thicker skin on the scalp means that Botox injections in this area will be more painful than injections on the face, where the skin is thinner. 'Considering the limited ability to stop enough sweating to make a real difference, the cost/benefit ratio isn't going to make sense,' he stated.

Ahora, algunas mujeres buscan usos no autorizados de este inyectable para prolongar la duración de sus peinados. Según Yahoo Beauty, este procedimiento está ganando popularidad entre las mujeres que quieren 'ir a SoulCycle sin que se les sude el pelo'. La destacada dermatóloga neoyorquina, Dra. Patricia Wexler, señala que una mejor calidad del cabello es un efecto secundario positivo del efecto del Botox en las glándulas sudoríparas. ¿Es esta una solución extrema para evitar el encrespamiento? Ahora se inyecta Botox en el cuero cabelludo para ayudar a las pacientes a mantener sus peinados por más tiempo. 'Funciona igual que las inyecciones para la hiperhidrosis', dijo a Dailymail.com. '[El Botox] inhibe específicamente las glándulas ecrinas'. El resultado de la reducción de la transpiración del cuero cabelludo es que las pacientes pueden notar menos encrespamiento y no tener que lavarse el pelo tan a menudo. La Dra. Wexler reconoce que el coste del procedimiento puede ser 'prohibitivo', pero lo recomendaría si una paciente lo consultara. 'Tiene pocos efectos secundarios si se administra con una dilución y dosis seguras', explica. 'Debe colocarse con cuidado a lo largo de la línea de crecimiento del pelo y en la zona frontal, donde el encrespamiento es más evidente'. Francesca Fusco dijo a Yahoo que 'varias mujeres a las que he inyectado la frente informan de una feliz reducción de la sudoración en la línea de crecimiento del pelo y en las sienes'. Además, la piel más gruesa del cuero cabelludo hace que las inyecciones de Botox en esta zona sean más dolorosas que las inyecciones en la cara, donde la piel es más fina. 'Teniendo en cuenta la limitada capacidad para detener la sudoración lo suficiente como para marcar una diferencia real, la relación coste/beneficio no tiene sentido', afirmó.

article_content: A magnitude 3.8 earthquake struck San Bernardino County in Southern California near the San Andreas Fault on Saturday morning. Authorities reported no major damage. The earthquake's epicenter was located two miles northwest of Devore, California. Residents in Devore told CNN affiliate KCAL that their homes shook, but authorities reported no damage. Seismologist Lucy Jones of the U.S. Geological Survey told KCAL that the quake was located very close to, but not on, the San Andreas Fault. John Bellini of the U.S. Geological Survey added that it was capable of knocking items from shelves and possibly cracking plaster. The USGS initially reported the magnitude as 4.1 before revising it to 3.8. The San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department in Rancho Cucamonga informed CNN that they received no reports of significant damage shortly after the earthquake. "It was a solid boom and everything shook," Tracie Thompson, a Devore resident, told KCAL. "None of the china moved or anything. It was over so quickly. It was really a harsh jolt to the house." Devore is approximately 55 miles northeast of downtown Los Angeles. The region is known as the Inland Empire, situated east of Los Angeles. CNN's Michael Martinez reported from Los Angeles, and Kara Devlin reported from Atlanta.

article_content: Tony Stewart's profession is driving in NASCAR races for millions of dollars a year, but his hobby is racing against amateurs on dirt tracks for trophies. Stewart, 43, started in go-carts when he was just 5 in Columbus, Indiana, located 50 miles south of the Indianapolis Motor Speedway. He rose through the ranks, winning the Indy Racing League championship in 1997 before moving to NASCAR two years later. He's won three championships in NASCAR's premier series -- the Sprint Cup -- and is a co-owner of his racing team. Other drivers started calling him 'Smoke' because of the smoke coming from his tires as he aggressively steered through turns on asphalt tracks. While burning rubber wore down tire tread needed late in a race, it contributed to his reputation as one of the most competitive drivers, both on and off the track. Sponsors pay significant amounts to display their logos on Stewart's No. 14 car because they know millions will watch it speed around the track multiple times in a single event, which occurs dozens of weekends a year. His controversial antics, including fights and heated exchanges, make him stand out among other personalities in the sport. Even the fans who boo him are watching. He often appears unshaven on race days, in contrast to more polished drivers who are careful with their words and actions to avoid alienating sponsors and fans. Winning, whether on NASCAR's asphalt or unsanctioned dirt, is Stewart's primary goal. He sacrifices tire tread for track credibility and dedicates great passion to his non-paying hobby, carried out at the risk of his lucrative professional driving career. Why one NASCAR champion loves dirt tracks. 'Being on a dirt track a lot of times is like being on a gravel road,' Stewart said in a 2006 interview. 'If you go just a little bit too fast the car's going to slide. If you hit the gas too hard, it spins the tires or kicks the rocks up. If you try to stop too fast, you skid, you lock up the brakes. That's what makes driving on dirt more technical.' When he won a dirt track race in Michigan last month, he tweeted to fans as if he'd won the Daytona 500: 'If you haven't heard already, I ran my sprint car tonight and won! Felt great to run it again. Was a 2nd place car but had a little luck :)' That 'little luck' referred to the driver of the lead car crashing. Stewart was leading a 30-lap dirt track race at Southern Iowa Speedway a year ago when his car flipped, breaking two bones in his right leg. It ended his NASCAR Sprint Cup season 15 races early, resulting in significant financial losses for him and his sponsors. The August 11, 2013, race at Watkins Glen, New York, was the first start Stewart missed in 521 NASCAR races since his 1999 debut at the Daytona 500. Ironically, he missed Watkins Glen again this year due to a dirt track tragedy on Saturday. Tony Stewart hits, kills driver at dirt-race track. Stewart hit and killed another driver, Kevin Ward Jr., during a sprint car race at Canandaigua Motorsports Park in Ontario County, New York. Video shows that Ward and Stewart appeared to make contact coming out of a turn, and Ward hit the wall and was knocked out of the race. Ward, 20, then exited his car and walked down the track toward the other racers, who had slowed for a yellow flag. Ward pointed a finger and appeared to be yelling. One car swerved to avoid him, but Stewart's right-rear tire appeared to hit him as he passed. 'There aren't words to describe the sadness I feel about the accident that took the life of Kevin Ward Jr.,' Stewart said in a written statement. Why Tony Stewart isn't likely to face charges. Veteran race fans remember a rookie driver who jumped out of his car during a NASCAR race in 1999 after another driver spun his car into him in Martinsville, Virginia. That driver was Tony Stewart. Stewart had traded bumps throughout the race with Kenny Irwin, who had been his dirt-track rival before they both moved up to NASCAR. But the last crash against the wall disabled Stewart's car. Stewart waited on the track for Irwin to circle around under a caution flag. Stewart threw his gloves at Irwin's car and jumped onto its right side while the car was still moving. Stewart's run-ins with other drivers are legendary, including after his car crashed with Matt Kenseth at Bristol Motor Speedway in Tennessee in 2012. Stewart waited in a driving lane on pit road for Kenseth's car to return to the track. Stewart threw his helmet at Kenseth as the car sped by. He told reporters later that he doesn't 'enjoy getting mad like that.' Stewart rushed after driver Joey Logano on pit road after a Fontana, California, race last year. He was angry that the younger Logano had blocked him from passing during a restart. Logano said he was just 'racing hard' because he thought he could win. Stewart has also had angry moments with fans and the media. He was investigated, though never prosecuted, for an alleged assault against a female fan at Bristol Motor Speedway in 2002, the year he won his first of three NASCAR championships. NASCAR officials fined Stewart $10,000 and ordered him to get anger management counseling for hitting a photographer after a bad race at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway in 2002. Stewart has removed himself from racing for the present in the aftermath of Ward's death. He will not compete in a dirt track race in Plymouth, Indiana, next Saturday as he had planned, the track announced Monday. He has not yet decided if he will race in the next NASCAR Sprint Cup event at Michigan International Speedway next Sunday, his spokesman, Mike Arning, said Monday. 'He is grieving, and grief doesn't have a timetable.' August was to have been a celebration for Stewart, the first anniversary of the dirt track wreck that changed his life. He tweeted this message to fans a week ago: '1yr ago today my life changed. Thank you to everyone that worked so hard to get me back to where I'm at today. It's your life, live it!'
translated_content: La profesión de Tony Stewart es conducir en carreras de NASCAR por millones de dólares al año, pero su pasatiempo es competir contra aficionados en pistas de tierra por trofeos. Stewart, de 43 años, comenzó en karts cuando tenía solo 5 años en Columbus, Indiana, ubicada a 80 kilómetros al sur del Indianapolis Motor Speedway. Ascendió de rango, ganando el campeonato de la Indy Racing League en 1997 antes de pasar a la NASCAR dos años después. Ha ganado tres campeonatos en la serie principal de NASCAR, la Sprint Cup, y es copropietario de su equipo de carreras. Otros pilotos comenzaron a llamarlo 'Smoke' (Humo) debido al humo que salía de sus neumáticos mientras conducía agresivamente en las curvas en pistas de asfalto. Si bien quemar goma desgastaba la banda de rodadura de los neumáticos necesaria al final de una carrera, contribuyó a su reputación como uno de los pilotos más competitivos, tanto dentro como fuera de la pista. Los patrocinadores pagan cantidades importantes para mostrar sus logotipos en el coche número 14 de Stewart porque saben que millones lo verán acelerar en la pista varias veces en un solo evento, lo que ocurre docenas de fines de semana al año. Sus controvertidas payasadas, incluidas peleas e intercambios acalorados, lo hacen destacar entre otras personalidades del deporte. Incluso los fanáticos que lo abuchean lo están mirando. A menudo aparece sin afeitar en los días de carrera, a diferencia de los pilotos más pulidos que tienen cuidado con sus palabras y acciones para no alienar a los patrocinadores y a los fanáticos. Ganar, ya sea en el asfalto de NASCAR o en la tierra, es el objetivo principal de Stewart. Sacrifica la banda de rodadura de los neumáticos por la credibilidad en la pista y dedica una gran pasión a su pasatiempo no remunerado, que lleva a cabo a riesgo de su lucrativa carrera como piloto profesional. Por qué a un campeón de NASCAR le encantan las pistas de tierra. 'Estar en una pista de tierra muchas veces es como estar en un camino de grava', dijo Stewart en una entrevista de 2006. 'Si vas un poco demasiado rápido, el coche se deslizará. Si pisas el acelerador demasiado fuerte, las ruedas patinarán o levantarán las piedras. Si intentas detenerte demasiado rápido, derraparás y bloquearás los frenos. Eso es lo que hace que conducir en tierra sea más técnico.' Cuando ganó una carrera en pista de tierra en Michigan el mes pasado, tuiteó a los fanáticos como si hubiera ganado las 500 Millas de Daytona: 'Si aún no lo han escuchado, ¡corrí mi auto de velocidad esta noche y gané! Fue genial volver a correrlo. Era un coche de segundo lugar, pero tuve un poco de suerte :)' Esa 'pequeña suerte' se refería al piloto del coche de cabeza que se estrelló. Stewart lideraba una carrera de 30 vueltas en pista de tierra en Southern Iowa Speedway hace un año cuando su coche volcó, rompiéndose dos huesos de la pierna derecha. Terminó su temporada de la Sprint Cup de NASCAR de 2013, 15 carreras antes, lo que resultó en importantes pérdidas financieras para él y sus patrocinadores. La carrera del 11 de agosto de 2013 en Watkins Glen, Nueva York, fue la primera carrera que Stewart se perdió en 521 carreras de NASCAR desde su debut en 1999 en las 500 Millas de Daytona. Irónicamente, volvió a perderse Watkins Glen este año debido a una tragedia en una pista de tierra el sábado. Tony Stewart golpea y mata a un piloto en una pista de carreras de tierra. Stewart golpeó y mató a otro piloto, Kevin Ward Jr., durante una carrera de autos sprint en Canandaigua Motorsports Park en el condado de Ontario, Nueva York. El video muestra que Ward y Stewart parecieron hacer contacto al salir de una curva, y Ward golpeó la pared y quedó fuera de la carrera. Ward, de 20 años, luego salió de su coche y caminó por la pista hacia los otros corredores, que habían disminuido la velocidad debido a una bandera amarilla. Ward señaló con el dedo y parecía estar gritando. Un coche giró para evitarlo, pero el neumático trasero derecho de Stewart pareció golpearlo al pasar. 'No hay palabras para describir la tristeza que siento por el accidente que le quitó la vida a Kevin Ward Jr.', dijo Stewart en un comunicado escrito. Por qué es poco probable que Tony Stewart enfrente cargos. Los fanáticos veteranos de las carreras recuerdan a un piloto novato que saltó de su coche durante una carrera de NASCAR en 1999 después de que otro piloto hiciera girar su coche contra él en Martinsville, Virginia. Ese piloto era Tony Stewart. Stewart había intercambiado golpes durante la carrera con Kenny Irwin, quien había sido su rival en la pista de tierra antes de que ambos ascendieran a la NASCAR. Pero el último choque contra la pared inutilizó el coche de Stewart. Stewart esperó en la pista a que Irwin diera la vuelta bajo una bandera de precaución. Stewart arrojó sus guantes al coche de Irwin y saltó sobre su lado derecho mientras el coche aún se movía. Los encontronazos de Stewart con otros pilotos son legendarios, incluso después de que su coche chocara con Matt Kenseth en Bristol Motor Speedway en Tennessee en 2012. Stewart esperó en un carril en la calle de boxes a que el coche de Kenseth regresara a la pista. Stewart arrojó su casco a Kenseth mientras el coche pasaba a toda velocidad. Más tarde, les dijo a los reporteros que no 'disfruta enojándose así'. Stewart corrió tras el piloto Joey Logano en la calle de boxes después de una carrera en Fontana, California, el año pasado. Estaba enojado porque el joven Logano le había impedido adelantar durante un reinicio. Logano dijo que simplemente estaba 'corriendo duro' porque pensó que podía ganar. Stewart también ha tenido momentos de enojo con los fanáticos y los medios. Fue investigado, aunque nunca procesado, por una presunta agresión contra una fanática en Bristol Motor Speedway en 2002, el año en que ganó su primer campeonato de NASCAR. Los oficiales de NASCAR multaron a Stewart con $10,000 y le ordenaron que recibiera terapia para el manejo de la ira por golpear a un fotógrafo después de una mala carrera en el Indianapolis Motor Speedway en 2002. Stewart se ha retirado de las carreras por el momento tras la muerte de Ward. No competirá en una carrera en una pista de tierra en Plymouth, Indiana, el próximo sábado, como había planeado; la pista lo anunció el lunes. Aún no ha decidido si competirá en el próximo evento de la Sprint Cup de NASCAR en Michigan International Speedway el próximo domingo, dijo su portavoz, Mike Arning, el lunes. 'Está de luto, y el duelo no tiene un calendario.' Agosto iba a ser una celebración para Stewart, el primer aniversario del accidente en la pista de tierra que cambió su vida. Tuiteó este mensaje a los fanáticos hace una semana: 'Hace un año, mi vida cambió. Gracias a todos los que trabajaron tan duro para que volviera a donde estoy hoy. ¡Es tu vida, vívela!'

article_content: In court on Thursday, a Florida Army veteran named John Orr, 39, accused of fatally stabbing a stranger, was revealed to have sent a text message admitting to the crime an hour after the deadly altercation. Orr is facing a second-degree murder charge for the October 2011 killing of 63-year-old Jon Wayne Joseph in Naples. Orr told police following his arrest that he acted in self-defense, claiming Joseph rammed him with a bicycle, pinned him to the ground, and bashed his head after a brief exchange of words. Investigators allege that Orr pulled out a pocketknife and stabbed Joseph 75 times. According to the Naples Daily News, Orr was covered in blood when arrested. Detective Robert Young, the lead investigator, read a text message in court that Orr sent to a friend: 'I think I just killed a guy, stabbed him.' Another text stated: 'This isn't good.' The jury also heard testimony from Joseph's girlfriend, Roseann Hannigan, who stated that on October 3, 2011, Orr approached her in the driveway as she and Joseph were drinking beer. Orr inquired about a friend named Bert Newcombe. Hannigan responded that no one by that name lived there. Orr apologized and began to leave. However, Hannigan overheard him saying 'bitch,' 'whore,' and 'liar.' Joseph, upon hearing the insults, got on his bike and pursued Orr. Hannigan testified that Joseph did not appear angry, only frustrated. Joseph's last words to her were: 'Hon, I'll be right back. I'm going to see what's going on.' She never saw him alive again. Orr's friend, Colby Meeks, testified that he was on the phone with Orr when Joseph confronted him, telling him never to return. Meeks said Joseph sounded 'confrontational,' and then he heard sounds of a fight. 'I could hear just, fighting basically,' Meeks said, 'and at that point, John said, you know, “Don’t ever try that trick on me again” and I heard a gasping voice say, “OK, I won’t, I won’t.”’ Orr previously claimed at a 2012 pre-trial hearing that Joseph, nearly 30 years older, pinned him down, bashed his head into the ground, and threatened to kill him. Orr's attorney, Mike McDonnell, attempted to invoke Florida's 'stand your ground' law to secure immunity for his client, arguing that Joseph was in control and Orr feared for his life. The judge rejected the motion because blood splatter evidence was inconsistent with Orr's account. Prosecutor Andreas Gardiner pointed out that the unarmed victim suffered 75 knife wounds, while Orr had no injuries supporting his story. Orr's attorney indicated that Orr will testify later in the trial. Orr could face a life sentence if convicted of second-degree murder. The trial is expected to conclude next Wednesday or Thursday, after which the jury will begin deliberations.

article_content: Some people won't touch food or drink that's just a day or two past its 'best before' date. But when divers found a 72-year-old bottle of coffee beans in a shipwreck, they couldn't resist brewing them – and were amazed to find they made a hot beverage with a unique taste. The beans were recovered from the wreck of the Sulina, a Romanian cargo ship that sank in the Black Sea after being struck by a Soviet torpedo during the Second World War. Water discovery: Divers found a bottle of coffee beans in the wreck of the Sulina, which sank in the Black Sea after being struck by a Soviet torpedo during the Second World War. Examination: A diver holds the bottle of coffee beans recovered from the wreck. Despite the ship's violent end, the bottle of beans was salvaged with the stopper intact. Not content with this extraordinary find, the divers decided to open the bottle and brew a cup of coffee that had been waiting 72 years to be experienced. Photographer and diver Andrey Nekrasov, 42, said: 'We brought up a dark green bottle that had been floating near the ceiling of the mess cabin.' 'We could hear something moving inside, like beads. When we opened it, we could smell the bitter aroma of coffee.' Brewing up: Coffee beans from the wreck being poured into a coffee grinder (left) and distributed, ready for a taste test (right). Taste test: Two divers sample the coffee, describing it as 'remarkably fresh' and 'very rich' but with a taste that was 'overcooked'. 'We ground the beans and made coffee. The coffee was remarkably fresh, despite its age. The taste wasn't perfect, but it was one of the most memorable coffee breaks of my life.' 'The coffee smelled very rich. The fact that it had been underwater in a sealed jar gave it an amazing backstory, making the taste unique and special. I would describe the taste as overcooked, as if it had been stewing for a long time.' The Sulina is so well preserved because it lies at 72 feet below the surface - the height of four double-decker buses - protecting it from wave action. Other ships from the same period that sank at depths of 40 to 50 feet have been broken apart by winter storms. Divers also found lightbulbs from the wreck, which they connected to an electricity supply and brought back to life. A diver examines a bench on the deck of the sunken ship. A diver peers through a porthole in the ship's cabin. Mr. Nekrasov said: 'Many of the items found on the ship serve as excellent advertisements for the companies that produced them, because they are still in good condition today.' 'We brought some of the lightbulbs up, cleaned them of salt, and connected them to a light fitting. They still light up, despite having been under pressure two or three times that of the atmosphere for more than seven decades.' Although the Sulina was primarily a cargo ship, it had 16 first-class cabins and a well-stocked wine cellar. Toilets in the wreck: According to the divers, the flush and other faucets still worked. A sink on the floor of the wreck, which still had taps that turned easily, according to the divers. Mr. Nekrasov said: 'When we discovered the wine cellar, we rubbed our hands in anticipation.' 'My co-divers dug in the silt for days, only to be rewarded by several broken or empty bottles that smashed when the ship sank. The bottles we did manage to salvage had not aged well and now contained a strong grape vinegar.' The Sulina, built in 1939 in Palermo, Italy, sank on May 29, 1942, after joining the Romanian naval fleet at the start of World War Two. The cargo ship was part of a convoy of Romanian and German ships traveling from Constantsa, Romania, to Nikolayev, Ukraine. The Sulina was carrying coal and ammunition. A diver examines the crest on the ship's bow, which rests 72 feet beneath the surface near the port of Odessa. The ship was hit at 9:30 pm by a torpedo fired by a Soviet submarine. The captain, Victor Mikhu, had previously been alerted to foam trails in the water, thought to be from a submarine periscope. The Sulina attempted evasive maneuvers, but the ship was struck below the waterline on the starboard side. Water flooded into the engine room so quickly that three mechanics on watch drowned before they could leave their posts. In total, 31 Romanians and 56 Germans were rescued from the vessel before it sank seven miles from the port of Odessa.
translated_content: Algunas personas no prueban comida o bebida que esté un día o dos pasada su fecha de 'consumo preferente'. Pero cuando unos buzos encontraron una botella de granos de café de 72 años en un naufragio, no pudieron resistirse a prepararlos, y se sorprendieron al descubrir que hicieron una bebida caliente con un sabor único. Los granos fueron recuperados de los restos del Sulina, un buque de carga rumano que se hundió en el Mar Negro tras ser alcanzado por un torpedo soviético durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Descubrimiento acuático: Buzos encontraron una botella de granos de café en los restos del Sulina, que se hundió en el Mar Negro tras ser alcanzado por un torpedo soviético durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Examen: Un buzo sostiene la botella de granos de café recuperados del naufragio. A pesar del trágico final del barco, la botella de granos se rescató con el tapón intacto. Entusiasmados con este extraordinario hallazgo, los buzos decidieron abrir la botella y preparar una taza de café que había estado esperando 72 años para ser bebida. El fotógrafo y buzo Andrey Nekrasov, de 42 años, dijo: 'Sacamos una botella verde oscura que flotaba cerca del techo del camarote de la tripulación.' 'Podíamos oír algo moviéndose dentro, como bolitas. Al abrirla, notamos el amargo aroma a café.' Preparación: Granos de café del naufragio vertidos en un molinillo (izquierda) y distribuidos, listos para la cata (derecha). Cata: Dos buzos prueban el café y lo describen como 'sorprendentemente fresco' y 'muy intenso', pero con un sabor 'pasado'. 'Molimos los granos e hicimos café. Estaba sorprendentemente fresco, a pesar de su edad. El sabor no era perfecto, pero fue uno de los descansos para tomar café más memorables de mi vida.' 'El café tenía un aroma muy intenso. El hecho de haber estado bajo el agua en un frasco sellado le daba una historia increíble, lo que hizo que su sabor fuera único y especial. Yo lo describiría como pasado, como si hubiera estado cociéndose a fuego lento durante mucho tiempo.' El Sulina está tan bien conservado porque se encuentra a 22 metros bajo la superficie (la altura de cuatro autobuses de dos pisos), lo que lo protege del oleaje. Otros barcos de la misma época hundidos a entre 12 y 15 metros se han destrozado por las tormentas invernales. Los buzos también encontraron bombillas del naufragio, que conectaron a la corriente y volvieron a encender. Un buzo examina un banco en la cubierta del barco hundido. Un buzo mira por un ojo de buey en la cabina del barco. Nekrasov comentó: 'Muchos de los objetos encontrados en el barco sirven como excelentes anuncios de las empresas que los fabricaron, porque se conservan en buen estado.' 'Sacamos algunas bombillas, las limpiamos de la sal y las conectamos a un casquillo. Siguen funcionando, pese a haber soportado una presión dos o tres veces superior a la atmosférica durante más de siete décadas.' Aunque el Sulina era principalmente un carguero, tenía 16 camarotes de primera clase y una bodega bien provista. Aseos en el naufragio: Según los buzos, la cisterna y otros grifos aún funcionaban. Un lavabo en el suelo del naufragio aún tenía grifos que se abrían con facilidad, según los buzos. Nekrasov relató: 'Cuando descubrimos la bodega, nos relamimos de gusto.' 'Mis compañeros buzos estuvieron días excavando en el limo, solo para encontrar botellas rotas o vacías que se hicieron añicos al hundirse el barco. Las pocas que pudimos rescatar no habían envejecido bien y ahora contenían un fuerte vinagre de uva.' El Sulina, construido en 1939 en Palermo (Italia), se hundió el 29 de mayo de 1942 tras incorporarse a la flota naval rumana al comienzo de la Segunda Guerra Mundial. El carguero formaba parte de un convoy de barcos rumanos y alemanes que viajaban desde Constanza (Rumanía) a Mikolaiv (Ucrania). El Sulina transportaba carbón y municiones. Un buzo examina el escudo de la proa del barco, que descansa a 22 metros bajo la superficie cerca del puerto de Odesa. El barco fue alcanzado a las 21:30 por un torpedo lanzado por un submarino soviético. El capitán, Victor Mikhu, había sido advertido de la presencia de estelas de espuma en el agua, que se creía que procedían del periscopio de un submarino. El Sulina intentó realizar maniobras evasivas, pero fue alcanzado por debajo de la línea de flotación en el lado de estribor. El agua inundó la sala de máquinas tan rápido que tres mecánicos que estaban de guardia se ahogaron antes de poder salir. En total, 31 rumanos y 56 alemanes fueron rescatados del buque antes de que se hundiera a once kilómetros del puerto de Odesa.

article_content: A leading economist has strongly criticized Labour leader Ed Miliband's proposal to cap energy bills, suggesting it could severely damage the UK's energy infrastructure. Angel Gurria from the OECD, warns that freezing energy prices could lead to energy companies going bankrupt and discourage vital investment. According to Liberum Capital, approximately £6.7 billion has been wiped off the value of energy company shares since Miliband's pledge. The CEO of Npower cautions about a possible energy shortfall and potential blackouts in the UK. Labour peer Lord Puttnam has voiced criticism of Ed Miliband's leadership. Reports indicate that Miliband is seeking counsel from prominent Blairite figures. Vincent de Rivaz, the head of EDF, has emphasized the necessity of significant infrastructure investment. Labour's energy spokesperson defends the proposed price freeze, citing alleged excessive profits by energy companies. The government's chief scientific advisor indicates shale gas might be a better fuel alternative. Cuadrilla claims a substantial shale gas discovery in Lancashire could potentially supply Britain for 50 years.
